new_items.name: Country
new_items.summary: A nation with its own territory, government and borders, drawn as a shape on the map.

new_items.name: Flag
new_items.summary: A piece of cloth with colours and symbols that stands for a country or group.

new_items.name: Border
new_items.summary: The line where one country ends and another begins, sometimes marked by rivers or fences.

new_items.name: Globe
new_items.summary: A spherical model of Earth showing the continents and oceans in their true shapes.

new_items.name: Equator
new_items.summary: The imaginary line around the middle of Earth, equally distant from both poles.

new_items.name: South Pole
new_items.summary: The southernmost point on Earth, on the high ice sheet of Antarctica.

new_items.name: Valley
new_items.summary: A low stretch of land between hills or mountains, often with a river along its floor.

new_items.name: Peninsula
new_items.summary: Land surrounded by water on three sides but still joined to the mainland.

new_items.name: Fjord
new_items.summary: A long, narrow sea inlet filling a steep valley carved out by an ancient glacier.

new_items.name: Archipelago
new_items.summary: A group or chain of islands scattered across a stretch of sea.

new_items.name: Wall
new_items.summary: A long defensive barrier built along a frontier to keep out invaders.

new_items.name: Temple
new_items.summary: A sacred building where people gather to worship, pray and celebrate holy days.

new_items.name: Palace
new_items.summary: A grand residence built for a ruler, filled with halls, gardens and ceremony.

new_items.name: Skyscraper
new_items.summary: A very tall building with many floors, made possible by steel frames and elevators.

new_items.name: Feast
new_items.summary: A large, festive meal shared by many people to mark a special occasion.

new_items.name: Festival
new_items.summary: A day or season of celebration with music, food, decorations and traditions.

new_items.name: Costume
new_items.summary: Traditional clothing worn to show cultural identity, often on holidays and special days.

new_items.name: Safari
new_items.summary: An expedition to watch wild animals in their natural habitat, especially in East Africa.

new_items.name: Africa
new_items.summary: The second-largest continent, home to 54 countries, the Sahara and the Nile.

new_items.name: North America
new_items.summary: The continent stretching from the Arctic to Central America, including Canada, the USA and Mexico.

new_items.name: South America
new_items.summary: The continent of the Andes and the Amazon, home to 12 sovereign countries.

new_items.name: Oceania
new_items.summary: The region of Australia, New Zealand and thousands of Pacific islands.

new_items.name: Antarctica
new_items.summary: The icy southern continent with no permanent population, set aside for science by treaty.

new_items.name: France
new_items.summary: A Western European country known for Paris, fine cuisine, wine and the Eiffel Tower.

new_items.name: Italy
new_items.summary: A boot-shaped Mediterranean peninsula, home of ancient Rome, the Renaissance and pizza.

new_items.name: Spain
new_items.summary: An Iberian country famed for flamenco, paella, fiestas and Moorish palaces.

new_items.name: Greece
new_items.summary: A Mediterranean country of islands and ancient ruins, birthplace of democracy and the Olympics.

new_items.name: Switzerland
new_items.summary: A mountainous Alpine country known for lakes, cheese, chocolate and clocks.

new_items.name: Norway
new_items.summary: A Scandinavian country of dramatic fjords, northern lights and the midnight sun.

new_items.name: Iceland
new_items.summary: A North Atlantic island nation of glaciers, volcanoes, geysers and hot springs.

new_items.name: Netherlands
new_items.summary: A low-lying European country of canals, windmills, tulips and bicycles.

new_items.name: Germany
new_items.summary: A central European country known for castles, forests, engineering and festivals.

new_items.name: Portugal
new_items.summary: A seafaring country on Europe's Atlantic edge, famous for explorers, fado and blue tiles.

new_items.name: Russia
new_items.summary: The world's largest country by area, spanning eastern Europe and northern Asia.

new_items.name: India
new_items.summary: A vast South Asian country of many languages, spices, festivals and ancient temples.

new_items.name: Nepal
new_items.summary: A Himalayan country between China and India, home to Mount Everest.

new_items.name: Thailand
new_items.summary: A Southeast Asian kingdom of golden temples, tropical beaches and street food.

new_items.name: Indonesia
new_items.summary: The world's largest archipelagic country, spread across more than 17,000 islands.

new_items.name: South Korea
new_items.summary: An East Asian country on the southern Korean Peninsula, known for K-pop and kimchi.

new_items.name: Cambodia
new_items.summary: A Southeast Asian kingdom, heart of the ancient Khmer Empire and Angkor.

new_items.name: Vietnam
new_items.summary: A long S-shaped Southeast Asian country of rice paddies, the Mekong Delta and pho.

new_items.name: Jordan
new_items.summary: A Middle Eastern kingdom of desert landscapes such as Wadi Rum and the rose-red city of Petra.

new_items.name: United Arab Emirates
new_items.summary: A federation of seven emirates on the Arabian Peninsula, known for desert and record-breaking skyscrapers.

new_items.name: Egypt
new_items.summary: A North African country along the Nile, home of the pharaohs, pyramids and the Sphinx.

new_items.name: Kenya
new_items.summary: An East African country of savanna, safaris, wildlife and long-distance runners.

new_items.name: Tanzania
new_items.summary: An East African country home to Kilimanjaro, the Serengeti and Zanzibar.

new_items.name: Morocco
new_items.summary: A North African kingdom of spice markets, desert, mountains and mosaic-tiled cities.

new_items.name: South Africa
new_items.summary: The country at Africa's southern tip, bordered by the Atlantic and Indian oceans.

new_items.name: Madagascar
new_items.summary: A huge island nation off Africa's east coast, home to lemurs found nowhere else.

new_items.name: Ethiopia
new_items.summary: An ancient East African highland nation, often called the birthplace of coffee.

new_items.name: Zimbabwe
new_items.summary: A southern African country named after the medieval stone city of Great Zimbabwe.

new_items.name: Canada
new_items.summary: The world's second-largest country, famous for lakes, forests, maple syrup and hockey.

new_items.name: Mexico
new_items.summary: A North American country of ancient pyramids, mariachi, tacos and colourful festivals.

new_items.name: Panama
new_items.summary: A narrow Central American country linking North and South America, famous for its canal.

new_items.name: Brazil
new_items.summary: South America's largest country, home to most of the Amazon, samba and football.

new_items.name: Peru
new_items.summary: An Andean country of Inca heritage, Machu Picchu and Lake Titicaca.

new_items.name: Chile
new_items.summary: A long, narrow Pacific country stretching from the Atacama Desert to Patagonian glaciers.

new_items.name: Argentina
new_items.summary: A large South American country of pampas, Patagonian glaciers, tango and asado.

new_items.name: Ecuador
new_items.summary: A South American country on the equator, which gave it its name, and home of the Galápagos.

new_items.name: Venezuela
new_items.summary: A South American country of Caribbean coast, Andes peaks and the world's highest waterfall.

new_items.name: Australia
new_items.summary: A country-continent of red outback deserts, coral reefs and unique wildlife.

new_items.name: New Zealand
new_items.summary: A Pacific island nation of fjords, mountains, volcanoes and Māori culture.

new_items.name: Fiji
new_items.summary: A South Pacific nation of over 300 islands, coral reefs and white beaches.

new_items.name: Flag of Japan
new_items.summary: The Hinomaru: a red disc on a white field, symbolising the rising sun.

new_items.name: Flag of France
new_items.summary: The Tricolore: three vertical bands of blue, white and red.

new_items.name: Flag of Italy
new_items.summary: Il Tricolore: three vertical bands of green, white and red.

new_items.name: Flag of Germany
new_items.summary: Three horizontal bands of black, red and gold.

new_items.name: Flag of Canada
new_items.summary: A red maple leaf on a white square between two red bands.

new_items.name: Flag of Switzerland
new_items.summary: A white cross on a red square, one of only two square national flags.

new_items.name: Flag of United States
new_items.summary: The Stars and Stripes: 13 red and white stripes and 50 white stars on blue.

new_items.name: Flag of United Kingdom
new_items.summary: The Union Jack, combining the crosses of England, Scotland and Ireland.

new_items.name: Flag of Greece
new_items.summary: Nine blue and white stripes with a white cross in a blue canton.

new_items.name: Flag of Norway
new_items.summary: A blue Nordic cross outlined in white on a red field.

new_items.name: Flag of Iceland
new_items.summary: A red Nordic cross outlined in white on a blue field.

new_items.name: Flag of Netherlands
new_items.summary: Three horizontal bands of red, white and blue.

new_items.name: Flag of Russia
new_items.summary: Three horizontal bands of white, blue and red.

new_items.name: Flag of India
new_items.summary: The Tiranga: saffron, white and green bands with a navy wheel of 24 spokes.

new_items.name: Flag of Nepal
new_items.summary: Two stacked crimson pennants with blue borders and white sun and moon.

new_items.name: Flag of China
new_items.summary: A red field with one large and four small yellow stars.

new_items.name: Flag of South Korea
new_items.summary: The Taegukgi: a red and blue yin-yang circle with four black trigrams on white.

new_items.name: Flag of Thailand
new_items.summary: Five horizontal stripes of red, white, blue, white and red.

new_items.name: Flag of Indonesia
new_items.summary: Two equal horizontal bands of red over white, called Sang Saka Merah-Putih.

new_items.name: Flag of Vietnam
new_items.summary: A yellow five-pointed star on a red field.

new_items.name: Flag of Tanzania
new_items.summary: Green and blue triangles split by a yellow-edged black diagonal band.

new_items.name: Flag of South Africa
new_items.summary: A sideways green Y edged in white and gold, with red, blue and black fields.

new_items.name: Flag of Morocco
new_items.summary: A green five-pointed interlaced star on a red field.

new_items.name: Flag of Panama
new_items.summary: Four quarters of white and colour, with one blue and one red star.

new_items.name: Flag of Chile
new_items.summary: White and red bands with a blue canton holding a single white star.

new_items.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
new_items.summary: The largest of the Giza pyramids, built as a tomb for Pharaoh Khufu around 2560 BC.

new_items.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
new_items.summary: A colossal limestone statue with a lion's body and a human head, guarding the Giza plateau.

new_items.name: Suez Canal
new_items.summary: An Egyptian canal linking the Mediterranean and Red seas, opened in 1869.

new_items.name: Eiffel Tower
new_items.summary: Paris's wrought-iron lattice tower, built by Gustave Eiffel's company for the 1889 World's Fair.

new_items.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
new_items.summary: A Gothic cathedral on Paris's Île de la Cité, famed for its rose window and gargoyles.

new_items.name: Palace of Versailles
new_items.summary: The opulent royal palace near Paris of Louis XIV, famed for its Hall of Mirrors.

new_items.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
new_items.summary: A tidal island in Normandy crowned by a medieval abbey.

new_items.name: Colosseum
new_items.summary: Rome's giant ancient amphitheatre, completed in AD 80 for games and spectacles.

new_items.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
new_items.summary: The bell tower of Pisa Cathedral, leaning since construction began in 1173.

new_items.name: Sagrada Família
new_items.summary: Antoni Gaudí's towering basilica in Barcelona, under construction since 1882.

new_items.name: Alhambra
new_items.summary: A palace and fortress complex in Granada, a masterpiece of Nasrid Moorish architecture.

new_items.name: Parthenon
new_items.summary: A marble temple to Athena on the Acropolis of Athens, completed in 438 BC.

new_items.name: Big Ben
new_items.summary: The nickname of the Great Bell in the clock tower of London's Palace of Westminster.

new_items.name: Stonehenge
new_items.summary: A prehistoric ring of standing stones on Salisbury Plain, built around 3000–2000 BC.

new_items.name: Hadrian's Wall
new_items.summary: A Roman stone wall across northern England, begun in AD 122.

new_items.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
new_items.summary: A fairy-tale 19th-century castle in Bavaria, built for King Ludwig II.

new_items.name: Brandenburg Gate
new_items.summary: Berlin's neoclassical gate, completed in 1791, a symbol of German reunification.

new_items.name: St. Basil's Cathedral
new_items.summary: A 16th-century cathedral on Moscow's Red Square, famous for colourful onion domes.

new_items.name: Great Wall of China
new_items.summary: A series of fortifications stretching across northern China, built over many centuries.

new_items.name: Forbidden City
new_items.summary: The vast imperial palace in Beijing, home to emperors for nearly 500 years.

new_items.name: Temple of Heaven
new_items.summary: A 15th-century complex in Beijing where emperors prayed for good harvests.

new_items.name: Taj Mahal
new_items.summary: A white marble mausoleum in Agra built by Emperor Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

new_items.name: Golden Temple
new_items.summary: Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar, the holiest gurdwara of Sikhism, covered in gold.

new_items.name: Kinkaku-ji
new_items.summary: Kyoto's Golden Pavilion, a Zen Buddhist temple covered in gold leaf beside a pond.

new_items.name: Himeji Castle
new_items.summary: Japan's finest surviving feudal castle, nicknamed the "White Heron Castle".

new_items.name: Tokyo Skytree
new_items.summary: A broadcasting and observation tower in Tokyo, 634 m tall, opened in 2012.

new_items.name: Angkor Wat
new_items.summary: A vast 12th-century temple complex in Cambodia, first Hindu and later Buddhist.

new_items.name: Grand Palace
new_items.summary: Bangkok's dazzling royal palace complex, home to the Temple of the Emerald Buddha.

new_items.name: Borobudur
new_items.summary: A 9th-century Buddhist temple in Java, built as a giant stepped stone mandala.

new_items.name: Gyeongbokgung
new_items.summary: Seoul's main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty, first built in 1395.

new_items.name: Petra
new_items.summary: An ancient city carved into rose-red sandstone cliffs by the Nabataeans.

new_items.name: Burj Khalifa
new_items.summary: The world's tallest building, an 828 m skyscraper in Dubai, opened in 2010.

new_items.name: Statue of Liberty
new_items.summary: A copper statue on Liberty Island in New York Harbor, a gift from France in 1886.

new_items.name: Empire State Building
new_items.summary: A 102-storey Art Deco skyscraper in New York City, completed in 1931.

new_items.name: CN Tower
new_items.summary: Toronto's 553 m communications and observation tower, completed in 1976.

new_items.name: Teotihuacan
new_items.summary: An ancient Mesoamerican city near Mexico City, with the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon.

new_items.name: Chichén Itzá
new_items.summary: A great Maya city in Yucatán, crowned by the stepped pyramid El Castillo.

new_items.name: Panama Canal
new_items.summary: An 82 km canal across Panama linking the Atlantic and Pacific, opened in 1914.

new_items.name: Christ the Redeemer
new_items.summary: The 30 m statue with outstretched arms atop Corcovado mountain in Rio de Janeiro.

new_items.name: Machu Picchu
new_items.summary: A 15th-century Inca citadel high on an Andean ridge above the Urubamba Valley.

new_items.name: Moai
new_items.summary: Monolithic human figures carved by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island.

new_items.name: Sydney Opera House
new_items.summary: A performing arts centre on Sydney Harbour with sail-shaped roofs, opened in 1973.

new_items.name: Great Zimbabwe
new_items.summary: The ruins of a medieval stone city in Zimbabwe, built without mortar.

new_items.name: Himalayas
new_items.summary: Asia's highest mountain range, home to Everest and most of the world's tallest peaks.

new_items.name: Mount Everest
new_items.summary: Earth's highest mountain above sea level, 8,849 m, on the border of Nepal and China.

new_items.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
new_items.summary: Africa's highest mountain, a dormant volcano in Tanzania rising to 5,895 m.

new_items.name: Andes
new_items.summary: The longest continental mountain range, running along South America's west coast.

new_items.name: Alps
new_items.summary: Europe's great mountain range, stretching across eight countries from France to Slovenia.

new_items.name: Matterhorn
new_items.summary: A pyramid-shaped Alpine peak of 4,478 m on the Swiss–Italian border.

new_items.name: Mount Fuji
new_items.summary: Japan's highest mountain, a 3,776 m volcano with a famously symmetrical cone.

new_items.name: Mount Vesuvius
new_items.summary: An active volcano overlooking the Bay of Naples, famous for burying Pompeii.

new_items.name: Uluru
new_items.summary: A giant sandstone monolith in central Australia, sacred to the Aṉangu people.

new_items.name: Grand Canyon
new_items.summary: A vast Arizona canyon carved by the Colorado River, up to about 1.8 km deep.

new_items.name: Victoria Falls
new_items.summary: A huge waterfall on the Zambezi River between Zambia and Zimbabwe.

new_items.name: Angel Falls
new_items.summary: The world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, dropping 979 m in Venezuela.

new_items.name: Niagara Falls
new_items.summary: A group of three waterfalls on the Niagara River between Canada and the USA.

new_items.name: Great Barrier Reef
new_items.summary: The world's largest coral reef system, stretching over 2,300 km off Queensland.

new_items.name: Sahara
new_items.summary: The largest hot desert on Earth, covering much of North Africa.

new_items.name: Lake Baikal
new_items.summary: A Siberian rift lake, the world's deepest and oldest freshwater lake.

new_items.name: Amazon Rainforest
new_items.summary: The largest tropical rainforest on Earth, spread over nine countries, mostly Brazil.

new_items.name: Galápagos Islands
new_items.summary: Volcanic Pacific islands of Ecuador, famous for giant tortoises and Darwin's studies.

new_items.name: Nile
new_items.summary: A great river flowing north through eastern Africa into the Mediterranean, the lifeline of Egypt.

new_items.name: Amazon River
new_items.summary: The giant river of South America's rainforest, with the greatest flow of any river.

new_items.name: Mississippi River
new_items.summary: A major US river flowing about 3,770 km from Minnesota south past New Orleans to the sea.

new_items.name: Yangtze River
new_items.summary: Asia's longest river, flowing about 6,300 km across China to the East China Sea.

new_items.name: Ganges
new_items.summary: A great river of northern India and Bangladesh, held sacred in Hinduism.

new_items.name: Danube
new_items.summary: Europe's second-longest river, flowing from Germany's Black Forest to the Black Sea.

new_items.name: Rhine
new_items.summary: A major European river that rises in the Swiss Alps and flows to the North Sea.

new_items.name: Thames
new_items.summary: The river flowing through London, the longest river entirely in England.

new_items.name: Seine
new_items.summary: The river through Paris, flowing past Notre-Dame and the Eiffel Tower to the English Channel.

new_items.name: Tiber
new_items.summary: The river of Rome, flowing from the Apennines to the Tyrrhenian Sea.

new_items.name: Volga
new_items.summary: Europe's longest river, flowing about 3,530 km through Russia to the Caspian Sea.

new_items.name: Mekong
new_items.summary: A great Southeast Asian river flowing from the Tibetan Plateau to Vietnam's delta.

new_items.name: Zambezi
new_items.summary: Southern Africa's longest east-flowing river, home of Victoria Falls.

new_items.name: Murray River
new_items.summary: Australia's longest river, flowing about 2,500 km through the south-east.

new_items.name: St. Lawrence River
new_items.summary: A great river linking the Great Lakes to the Atlantic, past Montreal and Quebec City.

new_items.name: Rio Grande
new_items.summary: A North American river that forms much of the border between Mexico and the USA.

new_items.name: Colorado River
new_items.summary: A south-western US river that carved the Grand Canyon over millions of years.

new_items.name: Río de la Plata
new_items.summary: The broad estuary of the Paraná and Uruguay rivers between Argentina and Uruguay.

new_items.name: Orinoco
new_items.summary: One of South America's longest rivers, flowing through Venezuela to the Atlantic.

new_items.name: Tagus
new_items.summary: The longest river of the Iberian Peninsula, flowing through Spain and Portugal to Lisbon.

new_items.name: Sushi
new_items.summary: A Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, seafood or vegetables.

new_items.name: Paella
new_items.summary: A Valencian rice dish cooked in a wide, shallow pan with saffron.

new_items.name: Tacos
new_items.summary: Folded corn tortillas filled with meat, beans, salsa and more, a Mexican staple.

new_items.name: Curry
new_items.summary: A family of spiced South Asian dishes with rich sauces built on spice blends.

new_items.name: Kimchi
new_items.summary: Korea's spicy fermented vegetable dish, usually made with napa cabbage and chili.

new_items.name: Pho
new_items.summary: Vietnam's fragrant noodle soup with clear broth, rice noodles and fresh herbs.

new_items.name: Pad Thai
new_items.summary: Thailand's stir-fried rice noodle dish with egg, tamarind, peanuts and lime.

new_items.name: Feijoada
new_items.summary: Brazil's hearty black bean and pork stew, served with rice and orange slices.

new_items.name: Ceviche
new_items.summary: Peru's dish of raw fish cured in lime juice with chili and red onion.

new_items.name: Poutine
new_items.summary: A Quebec dish of fries topped with cheese curds and hot gravy.

new_items.name: Fish and Chips
new_items.summary: Battered fried fish with thick-cut chips, a British seaside classic.

new_items.name: Couscous
new_items.summary: Steamed semolina granules served with stew, a staple of North Africa and Morocco.

new_items.name: Injera
new_items.summary: Ethiopia's spongy sourdough flatbread made from teff, used to scoop up stews.

new_items.name: Fondue
new_items.summary: A Swiss pot of melted cheese and wine, shared by dipping bread on long forks.

new_items.name: Moussaka
new_items.summary: A Greek baked dish of layered aubergine, spiced meat and creamy béchamel.

new_items.name: Peking Duck
new_items.summary: A Beijing dish of roast duck with crisp skin, served with thin pancakes and sauce.

new_items.name: Rio Carnival
new_items.summary: Rio de Janeiro's huge pre-Lent festival of samba parades, feathers and floats.

new_items.name: Day of the Dead
new_items.summary: Mexico's festival honouring departed loved ones with altars, marigolds and sugar skulls.

new_items.name: Oktoberfest
new_items.summary: Munich's giant folk festival, held most years since 1810.

new_items.name: Diwali
new_items.summary: The festival of lights celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs and Jains with lamps, sweets and fireworks.

new_items.name: Chinese New Year
new_items.summary: The Spring Festival marking the lunar new year, with red lanterns, dumplings and dragon dances.

new_items.name: Songkran
new_items.summary: Thailand's New Year festival in April, famous for joyful water fights.

new_items.name: La Tomatina
new_items.summary: A festival in Buñol, Spain, where crowds throw tomatoes at each other.

new_items.name: Hanami
new_items.summary: The Japanese custom of picnicking under blooming cherry blossoms in spring.

new_items.name: Inti Raymi
new_items.summary: The Inca Festival of the Sun, revived each June in Cusco, Peru.

new_items.name: Carnival of Venice
new_items.summary: Venice's pre-Lent festival famous for elaborate masks and costumes.

new_items.name: Kimono
new_items.summary: Japan's traditional T-shaped robe with wide sleeves, tied with an obi sash.

new_items.name: Sari
new_items.summary: A long, unstitched drape of fabric worn elegantly across India and South Asia.

new_items.name: Hanbok
new_items.summary: Korea's traditional dress with a short jacket and a full, high-waisted skirt.

new_items.name: Flamenco
new_items.summary: Andalusia's passionate art of song, guitar, dance and rhythmic hand-clapping.

new_items.name: Tango
new_items.summary: A dramatic partner dance and music born in Buenos Aires and Montevideo.
